title: Camera card: how should Live start and stop?

steps.headline: Which way of starting and stopping live video do you want on a camera card?
steps.notice: Pictures of each, with the camera's recordings list underneath. The next slide lets you press all three for real.
steps.risk: The Cameras tab is not affected; it starts every camera on its own.

variants.label: A play button on the picture
variants.summary: The camera card always has its picture area. A big round play button sits in the middle of it, with 'Watch live' under it. Press it and the live picture starts; a small Stop sits in the corner and the LIVE badge shows.
variants.risk: The card is taller when nothing is playing (a dark picture box with only a button on it), and the header has no control at all.

variants.label: A camera icon in the header
variants.summary: The word is gone: a small round camera-icon button at the top right of the card. Press it and it turns red with a stop square while live; press it again to stop.
variants.risk: An icon alone says less than a word; someone new has to hover to learn what it does.

variants.label: A Live / Recordings switch
variants.summary: A two-part switch under the header. 'Recordings' (the list) is the resting side; press 'Live' and the card shows only the live picture, press 'Recordings' to stop and get the list back.
variants.risk: You never see the list and the live picture together, and starting live is one press further from the name.

steps.headline: Press them: which one feels right?
steps.notice: Each is the real card with the pretend camera. Start live, stop it, press a recording.
steps.risk: The picture here is a moving test card, not a real camera.
